title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 10 vs. Los Angeles Rams
headline: Offense collapsed in a Week 10 loss to the Rams, and Trey McBride is being doubled on nearly every third down, a problem the coach expects to last the rest of the season.
summary: LaFleur said the only injury was Jordan Burch's knee, which will be tested Monday, and he would not call it good or bad yet. He defended first-time starting QB Carson, saying he did everything asked and was hurt by a pick right before halftime, a second pick on a misrun route by a back, and a fourth-down snap-count error. The offense had only about 34 snaps, went 0-for-6 on third down, ran for 34 yards and struggled against a strong Rams front, and LaFleur called the roster battered. He said Trey McBride is doubled on basically all third downs and that this will continue for the next seven weeks. He praised Simi Fehoko's catch on a deep throw. The defense gave up 46 carries for 202 yards and got burned by play-action. LaFleur framed the last seven weeks as a major evaluation of the roster, with injuries giving other players a chance to step up, and he said Michael Wilson was not in the lineup.

injuries.detail: Knee injury in the game. Tests Monday, and LaFleur would not say whether it is good or bad until then.
LaFleur said "Mike's not in there," meaning he did not play. No reason or timeline was given.

signals.claim: Defenses will keep double-teaming McBride on basically all third downs for the next seven weeks.
signals.note: Constant double coverage on third downs limits his upside, especially with a first-time starting QB and a depleted receiver group.
signals.quote: they just double trey on, on basically all third downs

signals.note: The coach singled out a deep throw to him as excellent, so he may be a rising target in a thin receiver room.
signals.quote: I thought the dagger that he threw to Simi was an excellent throw.

signals.claim: Burch's knee injury will be evaluated with tests on Monday.
signals.note: Defensive depth is a concern, and his availability for next week is unknown.
signals.quote: Not gonna even say if it's good or bad until I know more tomorrow.

topics.detail: LaFleur said Carson did everything asked, delivered intermediate throws well and looked sturdy. He blamed the two interceptions and the fourth-down failure on teammates' errors. Carson is not on the provided roster, so no signal is attributed to him.
About 34 offensive snaps, 0-for-6 on third down and 34 rushing yards against a top front. LaFleur said the team is banged up and called the result shared accountability.
The Rams ran 46 times for 202 yards and also beat the defense with play-action. LaFleur said the defense has to find a way to get off the field.
The final seven weeks are a roster evaluation with a focus on continuity. LaFleur said injuries open opportunities for new players and compared the situation to Michael Wilson's breakout last year.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 10 #SFvsDAL
headline: Cowboys lost 46-40 to the 49ers after the defense collapsed in the second half. Tyler Booker and DaRon Bland both have ankle injuries, with imaging pending, while George Pickens returned and looked strong.
summary: Schottenheimer called the second-half defense unacceptable. He blamed poor tackling and three explosive touchdown plays of 65+ yards, and said Dallas had led 17-16 at halftime. He wouldn't commit to a verdict on coordinator Christian Parker and said the staff will study the film. He explained that a cover-zero all-out blitz left Von Miller isolated on Christian McCaffrey for the final touchdown, and said Parker went with a call he liked that didn't work. He pointed to missed tackles, tackling too high, and poor eye discipline against reverses and naked boots, and said effort wasn't the problem. On offense, he praised Dak Prescott's competitiveness and was happy to have George Pickens back, saying Pickens is a playmaker once the ball is in his hands. Tyler Booker and DaRon Bland both have ankle injuries, and the severity will depend on X-rays and MRIs. KaVontae Turpin gutted it out, and Dallas limited his kick-return work because of the physical hits while keeping him on punt returns and offense. The team returns home next week.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury suffered in the game. The coach said the team needs imaging (X-rays/MRI) before it knows how much time he could miss.
Ankle injury suffered in the game. Severity unknown pending X-rays and MRI.
The coach said he 'gutted it out' and was kept off kick returns to avoid violent hits. He still returned punts and played offense.

signals.claim: Pickens is back from his hamstring injury and is a focal point of the offense when he gets the ball.
signals.note: His return was a highlight of the game and he produced early, which supports WR1 usage in a pass-heavy, high-scoring environment.
signals.quote: Awesome to have George back doing George things.

signals.note: The coach praised his toughness after he took early hits, and the offense kept scoring against a strong team.
signals.quote: maybe the greatest competitor I've ever been around.

signals.claim: Booker has an ankle injury, with his availability to be determined after imaging.
signals.note: An injury to an interior offensive lineman could hurt Dallas's offensive line and the running and passing game if he misses time.
signals.quote: book with the ankle and bland with the ankle.

signals.claim: Bland has an ankle injury, with his availability to be determined after imaging.
signals.note: His absence would thin the secondary, which already gave up several explosive plays.
signals.quote: book with the ankle and bland with the ankle.

signals.claim: Turpin will be limited on kick returns but stay on punt returns and offense.
signals.note: He keeps his offensive and punt-return roles, but his kick-return opportunities are reduced.
signals.quote: we wanted to limit the kick return ops.

signals.note: The coach described Miller as isolated one-on-one against McCaffrey on a cover-zero blitz that burned the defense. This reflects poorly on the coverage call more than on Miller himself.
signals.quote: tough match up for von you know because he's isolated one on one.

topics.detail: Schottenheimer said the defense tackled terribly in the second half: too high, not wrapping up, and not getting players on the ground. He said Dallas will fix it with drills and denied it was an effort problem.
Dallas allowed three touchdowns of 65+ yards, including a Deebo Samuel reverse and McCaffrey's cover-zero touchdown. The coach said explosive plays are what is killing the team.
Asked repeatedly about Parker, Schottenheimer wouldn't endorse or criticize him, saying he'd review the film and not change his answer.
He said the team keeps alternating wins and losses and playing one good half and one bad half. Dallas is now 1-4 at home this season.

title: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford & Blake Corum reflect on strong team performance in Sunday’s 34-6 Week 10 win over the Cardinals
headline: Blake Corum is hitting his stride as the Rams' run game becomes the identity, with Kyren Williams paired alongside him in new 20 personnel looks. The offensive line and tight ends are badly banged up heading into the bye.
summary: McVay was upbeat after the 34-6 win over Arizona, the Rams' fourth straight. He praised the defense for turnovers and for creating negative plays, naming Kamren Kinchens and Wesley Bailey. The offensive line was hit hard: Coleman Shelton and then Dylan McMahon left the game, and Beaux Limmer started at guard and slid to center. Eight linemen were needed, with David Quessenberry even used as a tight end. McVay said the tight ends are still banged up, so the staff added 20 personnel (Corum and Kyren Williams together) and other new looks to supplement their snaps. He called Corum outstanding and said he is catching his stride, with real twitch and explosiveness. He also credited Ronnie Rivers for closing out the game. Xavier Smith scored his first career touchdown on a screen that offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase suggested, and McVay said the best is yet to come for those role players. He said the run game has become an identity that sustains drives and helps on third down. Trent McDuffie returned, and McVay hopes the team gets healthier during the bye.

injuries.detail: Left the game hurt, forcing Dylan McMahon into center. McVay gave no diagnosis and said they will see who is available after the bye.
Came in at center after Shelton's injury, then also got hurt. No details given.
McVay said it was great to get him back on the field in this game.
McVay said the tight ends are 'still so banged up' and the staff wanted to supplement their snaps. No individual players were named.

signals.claim: Corum will keep a central role in a run-heavy offense that leans on him to close games.
signals.note: McVay says Corum is hitting his stride in a run game that has become the team's identity, which raises his fantasy value.
signals.quote: You can really feel the twitch, the explosiveness. He's seeing things really well.

signals.quote: two of our best players on the field at the same time

signals.note: He is a depth back who got late clock-killing work; this is not a clear sign of a bigger role.
signals.quote: Thought Ronnie ran really well at the end there.

signals.quote: Can't say enough about Bo Limmer.

signals.note: McVay singled out his turnover production, which is good for IDP value.
McVay praised him for getting into the backfield and for making a pick, which is good for IDP value.

topics.detail: McVay said the commitment to the run has become the team's identity. It lets them sustain possession, convert shorter third downs and close out games.

The Rams added 20 personnel and other new formations to supplement the banged-up tight ends and show Arizona something new on tape. Tight ends still contributed as blockers and got into the end zone a couple of times.
The Rams needed all eight of their offensive linemen after Shelton and McMahon both got hurt. Quessenberry played some as a tight end.
McVay said the defense is starting to hit its stride, with Trent McDuffie back and Wesley Bailey making a pick. He was not happy with the kicking game, saying they want to keep kicks in play.

McVay called the bye a chance to recharge and think up new ideas based on who is available. He said he does not view it as relief and wants the team healthier. He praised an unnamed player whose sack he called 'one of one'; the transcript does not make clear who he meant.

title: Klint Kubiak Postgame Presser - 11.15.26 | Week 10
headline: Brock Bowers left with an ankle injury and will be reevaluated Monday. The offense fell apart without him, and Kubiak says Fernando Mendoza's mobility should be used more.
summary: Kubiak opened by saying Brock Bowers has an ankle injury and will be reevaluated tomorrow. He didn't know how serious it is, only that it's an ankle. He said the offense's production changed noticeably once Bowers went out, and he blamed himself for not spreading the ball around better. Fernando Mendoza's first start got a positive overall review: he started well, was well prepared, and showed poise, maturity and leadership. Kubiak admitted the staff should have kept rolling Mendoza out in the second half after it worked in the first, and said his mobility gives the offense a different dimension. The offense was poor after halftime, including a three-and-out on the opening second-half drive. Seattle's pressure, including DB blitzes and off-schedule plays, led to six sacks, and the run game averaged under three yards per carry. Kubiak put much of that on himself and the staff. He said the defense took a step forward and kept the team in the game. Seattle's shell coverage also took away the deep ball.

injuries.detail: Left the game with an ankle injury. Kubiak said the team will reevaluate him tomorrow and has no sense yet of how serious it is.

signals.claim: Bowers will be reevaluated Monday for an ankle injury, and his availability for next week is uncertain.
signals.note: The offense's production dropped sharply once Bowers left, so his status is a key fantasy variable for the whole passing game.
signals.quote: Brock Bowers has an ankle

signals.claim: The offense will make more use of rollouts and Mendoza's mobility, including designed runs, in coming games.
signals.note: Mendoza's legs and extra rollout usage could raise his fantasy floor, especially if Bowers is limited and the passing game struggles.
signals.quote: His mobility helps. It gives us a different dimension

topics.detail: Raiders gave up six sacks. Kubiak credited Seattle's DB blitzes and off-schedule plays, said the team must help the quarterback better, and noted a rookie QB sometimes needs to throw the ball away.
The run game was under three yards per carry. It was positive in the first half but not sustained, and a run call to open the second half lost yardage. Kubiak took the blame.
Kubiak called the second half unacceptable and said the offense didn't give itself a chance to win. He said the staff expected more coming out of the tunnel.
Few deep shots were available because Seattle played shell coverage and took away the deep ball.
Kubiak thought the defense took a step forward and kept the team in the game, and said the offense needed to play complementary football.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "I'm Really Proud Of Our Team"
headline: Seahawks beat the Raiders and head into the bye with Abraham Lucas (ankle) and George Holani (knee) hurt, Sam Darnold's return unclear, and Drew Lock still the starter at 4-0.
summary: Macdonald was proud of the team after a win that he said showed progress in the run game, even though Las Vegas had the better plan in the first half. He praised the defense's second-half adjustments, including more blitzing that Devon Witherspoon turned into sacks. He praised Drew Lock's scramble touchdowns but wants the two turnovers cleaned up, along with red zone finishing. Abraham Lucas (ankle) and George Holani (knee) both left hurt, and the coach said he doesn't know how severe either injury is. Sam Darnold's status will be clearer after the bye, and he will need a significant amount of practice time before he can play. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was highlighted for making plays in every phase of the offense. Dante Fowler is getting more pass-rush chances now that games are producing passing situations, and Josh Jobe was praised for his tackling. Bobby Hart filled in for Lucas and played well, but Macdonald wouldn't commit to a plan for the offensive line if Lucas misses time. Players are off this week and return next Monday.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury; Macdonald said they don't know the degree yet and will put a plan together once they see how serious it is.
Knee injury; severity unknown. He went down late, and special teams personnel had to be shuffled on the final kickoff return.
Macdonald said the bye week is big and that Darnold needs a significant amount of practice time to play. The picture should be clear after the bye.

signals.claim: Darnold's availability will be decided after the bye, based on whether he can get enough practice time.
signals.note: Lock stays the starter until Darnold shows he can practice fully, so check practice reports closely after the bye.
signals.quote: We're going to want him to practice a significant amount of time

signals.claim: Lock remains the starting QB while Darnold is out.
signals.note: Lock is 4-0 as the starter with two scrambling TDs in this game, and the coach is fully behind him.
signals.quote: Drew's proven he's a great quarterback in our league.

signals.claim: Smith-Njigba will keep being used at every level of the offense: run game, quick game, intermediate and extended plays.
signals.note: He's over 1,200 yards, including 144 in the third quarter alone, and the coach sees him as a weapon in every phase.
signals.quote: he's a beast

signals.claim: Seattle will keep sending Witherspoon on blitzes when he is winning those rushes.
signals.note: Blitz-driven sacks add to his IDP value, and the coach called him a dynamite blitzer.
signals.quote: it was an adjustment in the game

signals.claim: Fowler's pass-rush role should keep growing as Seattle gets more passing situations.
signals.note: The coach said this is the role they envisioned for him, which is a boost for his sack upside.
signals.quote: this is more the role that that we envisioned for him

signals.note: Jobe made multiple tackles for loss from the perimeter, and the coach called him a physical corner who tackles well, which helps his IDP outlook.
signals.quote: Josh has shown that he's a physical corner

signals.claim: Hart is the fill-in at tackle if Lucas misses time, though the coach said no plan is set.
signals.note: Seattle's offensive line is thin with Charles Cross out and Lucas hurt, which could affect pass protection and the run game.
signals.quote: Bobby's done a great job on our Ready Squad all year

signals.note: He left with a knee injury of unknown severity, which puts his short-term role in doubt.

topics.detail: Macdonald thought the run game took a step forward but wanted to control the ball more late and convert first downs in must-run situations. He expects continued growth. Jadarian Price scored his first career touchdown, and Zach Charbonnet continues to gain momentum, according to a reporter.

With Holani hurt, other players had to step in on the last kickoff return. The coach called Tory Horton's play in the end zone incredible and credited the coaches for preparing players who hadn't practiced the plan much.
Seattle turned the ball over twice and struggled to finish drives in the red zone. Macdonald called these things the team needs to clean up.
The team is on the bye week. Players are off now and return next Monday.

title: Kyle Shanahan Reacts to Win Over Cowboys, Praises Kaelon Black
headline: Kaelon Black's long TD run earned him more work behind Christian McCaffrey, while Renardo Green left with a back injury and didn't return.
summary: Shanahan said Renardo Green's back was the only injury from the win over Dallas; Green left in the second half and didn't return. He praised the offense's big plays: McCaffrey's 74-yard TD (a blitz pickup that turned into an off-schedule throw from Brock Purdy), the late 66-yard TD with McCaffrey running a route against a defensive end, and Deebo Samuel's 70-yard reverse TD. He said the offense wasn't clean, with penalties, protection issues and a slow first half on the ground. Kaelon Black's big touchdown run got the staff to give him more work afterward, and McCaffrey then returned with a big third-down catch and several large runs. Purdy took five sacks and many hits but never told Shanahan he was hurt. Shanahan said the defense struggled to cover Dallas's receivers, didn't pressure enough and seemed gassed late. He credited Green and the player he called "Demo" (likely Deommodore Lenoir) for playing after missing a full week of practice. He was also pleased with the new receiver Keenan Allen in his first game, a week after arriving. Black's late fumble, a strip by Dallas's No. 92, was recovered, and Shanahan wants to review his ball security on film.

injuries.detail: Left in the second half with a back injury and didn't return. Shanahan gave no further update.
The coach said "Demo" and Renardo missed all week of practice and only did walk-through work Friday, but both played. The nickname is assumed to mean Lenoir.

The offense produced big numbers but had penalties and protection breakdowns, especially in the first half, from both blocking and Purdy holding the ball. Shanahan said Dallas has a better defense than people realize.
Shanahan said the team struggled to cover Dallas's receivers, didn't pressure the quarterback enough (one sack), and seemed gassed late as Dallas made it close.
Shanahan believed Fred Warner punched the ball out and that Malik Mustapha recovered it, but the review couldn't confirm a clear recovery. Dallas kept the ball.
